name: Raffaello D'Andrea

papers.title: KlaskTron-IL: A Contact-Rich Adversarial Imitation Learning Benchmark with a Validated Sim-to-Real Bridge
papers.abstract: KlaskTron is an open-hardware physical platform for two-player adversarial reinforcement learning, with a learned actuator model that supports zero-shot sim-to-real transfer of trained policies. Building on this platform, we contribute KlaskTron-IL: a multi-tier imitation learning dataset (80k human demonstration timesteps collected directly on the physical robot, 320k symmetry-augmented timesteps, and synthetic expert trajectories up to 5M steps generated by the zero-shot-validated PPO policy), a GPU-native Isaac Lab environment, and diagnostic baselines that expose three characteristic failure modes of standard IL methods under contact-rich adversarial dynamics: BC's data scaling plateau, GAIL's interpretable but unusable discriminator (Spearman $\rho = -1.0$ peg--ball proximity recovery with a logit gradient too flat to drive PPO), and an asymmetric BC-prior $\times$ reward-density interaction. Because the policy interface used throughout this paper is the same one the actuator model bridges to hardware, algorithms developed against these diagnostics are immediately deployable on the physical robot.
